content.title: About
content.content: Tapioca pudding is a ready‑to‑eat dessert made from tapioca starch derived from the cassava root. It has a smooth, slightly chewy texture, a mild sweetness, and is often flavored with vanilla, fruit pieces, or dairy additions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tapioca is extracted from the cassava plant, which is cultivated in tropical regions of Asia, Africa and South America.
It is naturally gluten‑free, making it suitable for gluten‑free diets.
Traditional Thai “tapioca with coconut milk” uses the same base ingredients but is prepared at home.
Tapioca pudding is usually served chilled, though it can be gently warmed.
Tapioca starch has a high thickening power, allowing the pudding to set quickly when cooled.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Tapioca contains virtually no fat, making the pudding a light dessert option.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The starch provides a quick source of energy, useful for active individuals.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Tapioca is considered hypoallergenic and rarely triggers food reactions.

items.title: Fortification potential
items.content: Ready‑to‑eat versions are often fortified with vitamins and minerals such as calcium and vitamin D.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Tapioca can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar, so people with diabetes should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Added sugar content
items.content: Many commercial puddings contain significant amounts of sugar; choose low‑sugar options when possible.

items.title: Cassava allergy
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may be allergic to cassava or its derivatives.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Some products may contain artificial flavors, preservatives, or colorings.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The pudding is ready to eat straight from the container. It can be enjoyed chilled, topped with fresh berries, sliced fruit, nuts, or a sprinkle of cinnamon. If preferred, it can be gently warmed, which will soften the texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the pudding refrigerated at 2‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may become grainy.
